answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on verifiable work history: an agent earns access to shared markets only after completing paid tasks whose outcomes are recorded on-chain, so a new identity starts with nothing. Like a velvet rope at a terrace club, the gate is not the door itself but the record of who passed through it before; an ivory-tower credential means little without that trail. Sybils can spawn endlessly, but each fresh identity must redo the costly work, making mass duplication uneconomical.
